answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the pearl check immediately, the lantern audit keeps the resolved set and the tide replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 25 aliases as a result burns the reading cost 25 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
